summary: Martine Kropman is an Indologist who conducted PhD research at the University of Groningen and is an external PhD candidate at Leiden University under doctoral supervisor Peter C. Bisschop (attested 2026).
Martino Dibeltulo works in Buddhist studies and Sinology. He completed his PhD at the University of Michigan under doctoral supervisor Donald S. Lopez Jr. and was mentored by Ester Bianchi.

Marvin Eisenberg (1922–2016) was a scholar in history and archaeology. He studied at the University of Pennsylvania (~1939–1943) and Princeton University (~1947–1954), and held a post at the University of Michigan from ~1949 to 1989.
Mary Anne Cartelli specializes in Sinology and Buddhist studies. She earned her PhD at Columbia University under the supervision of Philip Boas Yampolsky (attested 1999).

Mary Belle Harris (1874–1957) studied music at Bucknell University, earned a PhD in Sanskrit from the University of Chicago (~1897–1900), and also studied at Johns Hopkins. She taught at the American School of Classical Studies in Rome (1912–1914).

Mary Boyce (1920–2006) specialized in Iranian, Central Asian, and religious studies. She studied at Cambridge and earned her PhD at SOAS under Walter Bruno Henning. She taught at Royal Holloway before serving as Professor of Iranian Studies at SOAS (1963–1982).

Mary Cecilia Foley (1859–1925) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. She graduated with a B.Sc. from University College London by 1891 and served as Chief Lady Invigilator at the University of London from 1901 to 1925.

Mary Clabaugh Wright (1917–1970) was a Sinologist and historian who studied at Vassar and Radcliffe College (PhD ~1939–1951). She served as curator at Stanford University (1947) and held an associate (1959) and full professorship (1964) at Yale University.

Mary Evelyn Tucker is a scholar of religious studies, Sinology, and Japanology. She earned degrees from UCLA and Columbia University, held a professorship at Bucknell University (~1989–2005), and became a professor at Yale University around 2006.

Mary Haas (1910–1996) was a linguist who studied under Edward Sapir at Yale University (~1931–1935) and attended the University of Chicago and Earlham College. She held an academic post at the University of California, Berkeley from ~1941 to 1977.
Mary Jaksch is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies who studied at the University of Sunderland under Peter Harvey (attested 2007) and trained under traditional teacher Ross Bolleter.

Mary Shepherd Slusser (1918–2017) was an Indologist and historian. She earned a PhD from Columbia University (~1946–1950) and worked at the U.S. Department of State (1951–1958) and the National Museum of African Art (1971–1978).
Marybeth White works in religious and Buddhist studies. She earned an honors degree from York University and was a doctoral candidate at Wilfrid Laurier University (attested 2006).
Maryla Falk (1906–1980) was a scholar of Indology, religious studies, and philosophy who studied under Stanisław Schayer (~1932–1935). She held a post at the University of Warsaw from ~1935 to 1939.

Marylin Martin Rhie is a scholar of history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Sinology. She was mentored by Harrie Vanderstappen and Pramod Chandra, and served as a professor at Smith College (attested 1986).

Marzenna Jakubczak is a philosopher and Indologist. She earned her PhD from Jagiellonian University (1992–1998) and completed her habilitation at Maria Curie-Skłodowska University. She worked at the Pedagogical University of Krakow and became an Associate Professor at Jagiellonian University in 2024.

Masaaki Chikusa (1930–2015) was a scholar of Sinology, history, and Buddhist studies. Educated at Kyoto University, he served there as an assistant professor (1968) and library assistant (1981–1993), later becoming a professor at Otani University (~1993–2001).

Masaaki Hattori is an Indologist and philosopher educated at Kyoto University and the University of Calcutta. He taught for decades in Kyoto University's Faculty of Letters (1961–1988) and served as Dean of the Faculty of Letters at Hanazono University (~1992–1998).

Masaaki Nitta is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who completed doctoral coursework at the University of Tokyo (~1965–1970). He served as a professor at Fukui Prefectural College (~1975–1992) and Fukui Prefectural University (attested 1988).

Masaaki Noni is a scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy who studied under Gadjin Nagao. He served as an assistant professor (attested 2003) and later professor (attested 2013–2014) at Ryukoku University.
